subject: Status update — Traffic diversion to fallback region causing elevated tail latency
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 May 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Status update — Traffic diversion to fallback region causing elevated tail latency

Hi Claire / Stellaris team,

Quick note to let you know we’ve identified an upstream networking congestion event affecting our US-West edge POPs. Summary:
- Impact: elevated p95/p99 generation latency for some hosted inference requests routed to US-West. A subset of requests experienced 502 retries and longer tail latency.
- Scope: ~3% of traffic from US-West customers between 09:50–11:00 PDT; your traffic showed a measurable p99 uplift during that window.
- Immediate mitigation: we initiated automated traffic diversion to our US-East fallback pool at ~10:02 PDT which prevented a broader outage but caused higher tail latencies while caches re-warmed.

What we’re doing now:
- Ops bridge established (link in follow-up) and network engineering is working with our cloud provider to clear the congestion.
- We’re preserving request traces and token-level latency logs for auditing and will share an incident timeline.
- If you see any production failures on your side (errors or retries), please reply and include request IDs if available.

We expect elevated p99/p95 to persist 30–90 minutes while routing stabilizes and caches populate. We’ve opened an incident on the status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RI-2025-0504-edge-diversion.

Attachments: incident-timeline.csv (progressively updated)

I’ll follow up with a short post-incident summary and any recommended mitigations (e.g., warmup prefixes, routing pinning) once we have the full timeline.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident update — RI-2025-0504 edge traffic diversion (final)

Hi Claire and Stellaris team,

Thanks again for your patience while we investigated yesterday’s routing incident. Below is a concise post-incident summary and next steps.

Summary:
- Timeline: At ~09:50 PDT on 2025-05-04 we observed a sudden increase in packet loss on provider BGP sessions into our primary US-West POP. Between 09:50–10:02 PDT, error rates and retries increased; at 10:02 PDT our routing policy diverted affected prefixes to US-East. Normalizing traffic and cache warm-up completed by ~10:45 PDT.
- Impact: ~3% of global hosted traffic experienced elevated p95/p99. Stellaris saw increased p99 and a small number of 502 retries (we matched request IDs reported to entries in our logs). Dedicated pools that were pinned to a single POP (no multi-region fallback) were not impacted; any dedicated customers that allowed fallback saw elevated tails but no sustained outages.
- Root cause: transient provider-side peering congestion combined with a high-volume burst from a noisy tenant. We attribute the outage to routing and peering instability rather than service-level software faults.

Actions completed:
- Traffic diversion to US-East and targeted rate-limit on noisy prefixes (automatic fallback prevented full outage).
- Circuit claims and peering tickets opened with the provider; they confirmed packet drops during the window and applied route adjustments.
- Preserved and delivered full request traces and token-level latency logs to your team.

Attached: postmortem-draft.md (short incident write-up), incident-timeline.csv (detailed timestamps), ops-bridge-log-snippet.txt (selected logs).

SLA / Credits: Rishi will follow up separately regarding SLA calculus for the event window and any proactive credit offer. Our current stance is to evaluate credits against the measured impact window and your contract terms; we’ll offer a clear calculation and recommended goodwill package within 48 hours.

Recommended mitigations for Stellaris:
- Consider multi-region routing pin for Dedicated+ workloads that require strict tail-latency SLOs.
- Pre-warm critical prefixes during major launches to avoid cache-penalty induced tail spikes when diverted.
- Enable request-level graceful retry logic with jitter on client side for transient 502s.

If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical follow-up to walk through the timeline and logs. Would tomorrow at 10:00 PDT work?

Apologies for the disruption — we’re updating our monitoring and routing heuristics to reduce recurrence risk.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
